title: Different instruments, the same chord: the comb of resonances and the first-order phase for Dirichlet L-functions with complex characters, the cyclotomic union, and the robustness of the main resonance of study VI - a reproducible numerical study VII
description: Seventh study of the series (study I: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23815328; study II: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23928017; study III: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23991165; study IV: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24094318; study V: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24256378; study VI: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24381946). Study VI measured a comb of resonances in the variance of the windowed sums sum g x^(i gamma) over the zeros of zeta and of Dirichlet L-functions with real characters, in agreement with the two-point functions of Bogomolny and Keating. Here the measurement is extended to complex characters, and the question is what depends on the character and what only on its modulus. Every rule was recorded before the zeros were computed or, for the later additions, before the quantity was evaluated. On 1,296,658 newly computed zeros of 16 Dirichlet L-functions modulo 5, 7, 13, 15 and 21 between heights 36,000 and 80,000 (twelve with complex characters and four that complete the families modulo 15 and 21): (1) for the twelve L-functions with complex characters the comb depends on the modulus only - mean z^2 over 201 points 0.13-0.25 against the two-point function with the Euler factors of p | q removed and 11.5-49 against GUE without arithmetic, with the same comb for all 18 pairs of L-functions of one modulus; (2) the first order carries the phase of chi(p): the first Fourier coefficient of {gamma ln p/2pi} equals -w chi(p) ln p/sqrt p to 5.2e-5 in 56 combinations of these L-functions and primes, and the conjugate phase is excluded; (3) in the union of all characters of a modulus, which is the set of zeros of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(zeta_q) for q = 5, 7, 15, 21 (up to 947,573 zeros), a prime sounds only in the harmonics that are multiples of its order modulo q; (4) L-functions of one modulus share their primes, and the cross-covariance of their windowed sums equals the prime trace with the relative phase chi_a conj(chi_b); (5) the number variance saturates at a level set by the modulus; (6) the main resonance of study VI holds for another window, six error estimates and the full covariance of the scan, with GUE between 12 and 69 errors away depending on the error estimate. Three blind tests turn this into a use: from the zeros alone the modulus and the character, the primes dividing the modulus, and the orders of 16 primes in four cyclotomic fields were identified correctly, 16 of 16 in each test. Three further measurements connect the data with random matrices: the pair correlation of each L-function up to three mean spacings follows the two-point function of Bogomolny and Keating (chi^2 per bin 0.78-1.86) and not GUE alone (6.3-16.5); the spacings of the unions agree with a superposition of independent GUE spectra, one for each character, to 0.010 in the density, with a small deficit of the smallest spacings; and the deviation from GUE fades with height as predicted: between the bands 36,000-80,000 and 400,000-420,000 (178,844 further zeros) its size falls to 0.719 +- 0.021 of its value, against 0.727 predicted. A count test of Turing type found two pairs of close zeros that the search grid had stepped over; they were repaired before the evaluation. The one wrong reading outside the tests, the order of 11 in Q(zeta_21), is explained by the resolution of the band: near 11^5 the union hears the prime 161,071 twenty steps away. All 18 hypotheses are SUPPORTED. The statements tested in (2)-(4) are theorems or direct consequences of them; the two-point function behind (1), (5), (6) and the pair correlation is a conjecture. What is added is data for complex characters with null models and errors, zeros that did not exist when the rules were written, and the blind tests. Agreement is numerical support, not a proof; nothing here bears on the Riemann hypothesis. Article in English and Czech (PDF, DOCX, LaTeX, Markdown), 9 figures, the results files with every number of the article, an independent check that recomputes the statistics and the 18 verdicts from them, the rules recorded beforehand with their ten dated addenda, the manifests with the SHA-256 of every window of zeros, and the scripts as they were run. Text, figures and data CC BY 4.0, code MIT.
